**Steps to Reproduce**
op-reth binary is built from source using the latest git release `op-reth/v2.0.0` and the command:

`export CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=32 && RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native" cargo build --bin op-reth --profile maxperf --features jemalloc`


The bedrock state snapshot is downloaded from: https://datadirs.optimism.io/

```op-reth init-state --without-ovm --chain optimism --storage.v2 --datadir /home/optimism/.reth /data/pre-bedrock/op-mainnet-pre-bedrockstate```

topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: migrate tests (op-e2e L2 call sites, wait.go split, delete op-e2e/opgeth, audit op-devstack/sysgo)
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #20257. See plan §12, §13 in the op-geth decoupling doc (PR #19767).

## Goal

Migrate the integration/acceptance test layer to work with upstream go-ethereum. `op-acceptance-tests` is already half-decoupled (uses `op-devstack` DSL, zero direct `ethclient` imports) — improvements to `apis.EthClient` ripple through automatically. Main work is in `op-e2e` and `op-devstack/sysgo`.

## Scope

### `op-e2e/e2eutils/geth/wait.go` — split into header-only + full-block variants

These helpers use only standard go-ethereum APIs (no OP-Stack specifics), but `WaitForBlock` / `WaitForBlockToBeSafe` / `WaitForBlockToBeFinalized` transitively call `BlockByNumber`, which fails on L2 due to deposit-tx decoding.

Most callers discard the returned `*types.Block` (`_, err := geth.WaitForBlock(...)`). Plan:
- Add `WaitForBlockHeight(num, client)` returning `*types.Header` via `HeaderByNumber` — L2-safe even under upstream.
- Keep `WaitForBlock` for the few callers that read block body fields; migrate it to an `apis.EthClient`-backed impl.
- `WaitForTransaction` return type → `*optypes.Receipt` (ripples from #20264).
- `WaitUntilTransactionNotFound`: callers use non-deposit user txs; document and keep, migrate if needed.

### Direct L2 block/tx call sites in op-e2e (19 sites, 9 files)

Migrate to `apis.EthClient` or header-only variant:
- `op-e2e/actions/proofs/isthmus_fork_test.go` (3 sites)
- `op-e2e/actions/upgrades/ecotone_fork_test.go` (3 sites)
- `op-e2e/actions/helpers/user.go` (2 sites, `CrossLayerUser`)
- `op-e2e/faultproofs/cannon_benchmark_test.go` (1 site)
- `op-e2e/interop/interop_test.go` (1 site, `BlockByHash`)
- `op-e2e/system/bridge/validity_test.go` (1 site)
- `op-e2e/system/conductor/system_adminrpc_test.go` (3 sites)
- `op-e2e/system/fees/*.go` (3 sites)
- `op-e2e/system/verifier/legacy_pending_test.go` (2 sites)

### `op-e2e/system/e2esys.SystemConfig.L2Client`

Change from `*ethclient.Client` to `apis.EthClient`.

### `op-devstack/sysgo/` audit

Direct `ethclient.Dial` / `ethclient.NewClient` calls in ~7 files (mostly L1 contract deployment / faultproof game setup). Per-file audit: L1 callers stay on `*ethclient.Client` (safe); any L2 callers migrate to `op-service/sources.EthClient`.

### Delete `op-e2e/opgeth/`

This package exercises op-geth engine internals intentionally. Equivalent tests against op-reth will be introduced separately (tracked outside this issue). Delete the package as part of the decoupling.

## Dependencies

Blocked on: #20264 (`apis.EthClient` return-type changes and sources deposit-tx decoding).

topIssues.title: op-acceptance-tests: remove every SkipOnOpReth skip
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
**Goal:** remove every [`SkipOnOpReth`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/694bfc5a7764ee9e7c2ea2d573bfcaac8ff4d2db/op-devstack/sysgo/mixed_runtime.go#L66-L71) skip. Each test should either run on op-reth or be deleted with a stated argument.

op-geth is EOL as of Karst, and CI runs acceptance tests only with `l2_el_kind: op-reth` ([main.yml#L1980-L1983](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/694bfc5a7764ee9e7c2ea2d573bfcaac8ff4d2db/.circleci/continue/main.yml#L1980-L1983), [#L2679](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/694bfc5a7764ee9e7c2ea2d573bfcaac8ff4d2db/.circleci/continue/main.yml#L2679), [#L2702](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/694bfc5a7764ee9e7c2ea2d573bfcaac8ff4d2db/.circleci/continue/main.yml#L2702)). So every skipped test is currently dead coverage. Most of the skips came in with #19787, when op-reth was first run against all acceptance tests.

The inventory below covers every `SkipOnOpReth` call in `op-acceptance-tests`, `op-devstack` and `op-e2e`; there is no other EL-kind skip helper. Verdicts were reached by reading the tests, not by running them:
- **(a)** needs an op-reth capability or devstack primitive
- **(b)** asserts op-geth-only behaviour
- **(c)** the skip looks stale

### 1. EL resync: needs an EL-wipe primitive — (a)

These tests force a resync by stopping the verifier EL. They rely on "Since the sysgo EL uses in-memory storage this also wipes its database", which is true only for op-geth. op-reth's sysgo datadir is a per-node temp dir that persists across Stop/Start ([mixed_runtime.go#L382-L389](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/694bfc5a7764ee9e7c2ea2d573bfcaac8ff4d2db/op-devstack/sysgo/mixed_runtime.go#L382-L389), [#L423](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/694bfc5a7764ee9e7c2ea2d573bfcaac8ff4d2db/op-devstack/sysgo/mixed_runtime.go#L423)). On op-reth the restarted node therefore never resyncs, and the "peering issue" reasons are misleading.

- [`TestELSyncSafeRetractedByOffset`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/694bfc5a7764ee9e7c2ea2d573bfcaac8ff4d2db/op-acceptance-tests/tests/sync/elsync/offset_el_safe/sync_test.go#L26-L41): "not supported (peering issue)".
- [`TestTruncateDatabaseOnELResync`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/694bfc5a7764ee9e7c2ea2d573bfcaac8ff4d2db/op-acceptance-tests/tests/safeheaddb_elsync/safeheaddb_test.go#L27-L53): "not supported (peering issue)". The quoted error is `PeerWith` timing out after the restart.
- [`TestPreserveDatabaseOnCLResync`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/694bfc5a7764ee9e7c2ea2d573bfcaac8ff4d2db/op-acceptance-tests/tests/safeheaddb_clsync/safeheaddb_test.go#L15-L55): same reason and same `PeerWith` timeout.
- [`TestCLUnsafeNotRewoundOnInvalidDuringELSync`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/694bfc5a7764ee9e7c2ea2d573bfcaac8ff4d2db/op-acceptance-tests/tests/sync/elsync/gap_clp2p/sync_test.go#L49-L71): "not supported". It wipes the EL "to start from genesis", and the quoted failure is the EL advancing when it should not.

Needed:
- An op-devstack primitive that restarts an op-reth L2 EL from a fresh datadir, or an explicit `L2ELNode` wipe.
- `PeerWith` must work reliably against a restarted op-reth. It gets a new port (`--port=0`) but keeps its p2p key; that this causes the timeout is inferred, not verified.

These matter more now: the EL-sync action tests in `op-e2e/actions/sync` are being removed as part of #20257 (the op-reth-test-engine stack has no devp2p). That leaves these sysgo tests as the end-to-end coverage of op-node EL resync. The completion-head logic (offset, safedb) is unit-tested in `op-node/rollup/engine`.

### 2. Asserts that non-canonical blocks are readable by hash — (b) for the assertion, the rest likely passes

Both tests fail on op-reth with "failed to determine block-hash … could not get payload: not found". They expect a block that `engine_newPayload` executed but no forkchoice update canonicalized to be served by `eth_getBlockByHash`. op-geth does this because it persists side-chain blocks. reth keeps executed side-chain blocks in the engine tree, which RPC doesn't serve. The Engine API does not require either behaviour.

- [`TestVerifierManualSync`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/694bfc5a7764ee9e7c2ea2d573bfcaac8ff4d2db/op-acceptance-tests/tests/sync/manual/sync_test.go#L16-L64): drop the by-hash check before FCU (L63-L64) and unskip. The rest (newPayload VALID, not canonical by number until FCU, then canonical) is EL-agnostic.
- [`TestL2ELP2PCanonicalChainAdvancedByFCU`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/694bfc5a7764ee9e7c2ea2d573bfcaac8ff4d2db/op-acceptance-tests/tests/sync/elsync/gap_elp2p/sync_test.go#L58-L143): beyond the by-hash check ([L122](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/694bfc5a7764ee9e7c2ea2d573bfcaac8ff4d2db/op-acceptance-tests/tests/sync/elsync/gap_elp2p/sync_test.go#L122)), it documents op-geth skeleton-sync internals: whether SYNCING payloads are retained, and expected geth log lines. It tests the EL, not op-node, and largely overlaps `TestELP2PFCUUnavailableHash` and `TestSafeDoesNotAdvanceWhenUnsafeIsSyncing_NoELP2P` in the same file, which already run on op-reth. Candidate for deletion, or for cutting down to spec-mandated semantics (FCU with missing ancestors returns SYNCING, then VALID once peered).

### 3. Hardfork-transition sync — (a), cause unidentified

- [`TestSyncTesterHardforks`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/694bfc5a7764ee9e7c2ea2d573bfcaac8ff4d2db/op-acceptance-tests/tests/sync_tester/sync_tester_hfs/sync_tester_hfs_test.go#L37-L47): "not supported". The chain activates Bedrock through Jovian sequentially after genesis, and the quoted failure is that unsafe never advances. This is not op-geth-only behaviour: it covers running a chain through in-chain fork activations, which op-reth must handle. It needs an investigation into whether the cause is the op-reth sequencer at an activation or the sync-tester read path against op-reth.

topPRs.title: kona-peers,kona-disc!: Save the bootstore reliably
topPRs.author: aakoshh
topPRs.body:
### What

kona-node now saves its bootstore, saves it safely, and stops at startup when it can't, instead of running with a store it never saves. First PR of a stack for #23767; the next one changes *what* the bootstore saves.

For operators:
- The bootstore is saved at the default path, `~/.kona/<chain_id>/bootstore.json`, or at `--p2p.bootstore`. A missing file and its directory are created at startup.
- The node doesn't start if the bootstore file can't be read, isn't a JSON list of records, or is missing and can't be created. Entries that aren't node records are logged at WARN and dropped.
- The file is replaced atomically, only when its records changed, with the mode a newly created file gets.
- New counter `kona_node_discovery_dropped_enrs`: session records dropped because the channel to gossip was full. `kona_node_enr_store_time` now records only saves that wrote the file.
- The `kona-node` docker recipe keeps the bootstore in the node's home: its `kona_data` volume is mounted at `/home/app`, and `--p2p.bootstore` is gone.

BREAKING CHANGE: kona-node no longer starts when its bootstore can't be read, isn't a JSON list of records, or is missing and can't be created; before, it silently kept the records in memory and lost them at every restart. This applies to the default path too, so a node without `--p2p.bootstore` needs a writable home directory. Point `--p2p.bootstore` at a file, not a directory (such as `/db/bootstore.json` instead of `/db`), delete a file that isn't a bootstore, or pass `--p2p.no-bootstore`. In the kona-peers and kona-disc APIs, `BootStore::open`, `BootStore::in_memory` and `BootStoreFile::path` replace the `From`/`TryInto` conversions, `Default`, and the public fields; `BootStore::sync` returns whether there were changes; `merge` and `valid_peers` are gone; `Discv5Driver::bootstore` is an opened `BootStore`.

### Why

The bootstore usually wasn't saved at all. A failed open fell back to a store kept only in memory, without a log. Nothing created the default path's directory, and our docker recipes passed a directory as the path, so after a restart the node only had its bootnodes to start from; #24094 found that on Sepolia only one operator's built-in bootnodes answer. Where a file was saved, it was rewritten every minute by truncating it first, so a reader could see it empty and a crash left it empty. The driver also handed records to gossip from spawned tasks that waited for room in the channel, which piled up while gossip fell behind, and inbound sessions decide how many there are.

### How

- `BootStore` is a path, a private `Records` type with just the file's contents, and a dirty flag. `open` only reads, so that tests and tools can read the file while the node saves it. `Discv5Builder::build` opens it and saves it, which creates a missing file, so the node finds out at startup whether it can.
- Saves write a temporary file next to the bootstore, `fsync` it and rename it over the bootstore, on a blocking thread that the driver waits for.
- Records go to gossip with `try_send` from the driver loop. Saved records are shuffled, so each store interval gets a different part of them through, and fill at most half of the channel, leaving the rest for session records, which are handed over only once.

### Caveats

- An existing, valid bootstore in a directory the node can't write doesn't stop it from starting; every save then fails with a WARN. A file that exists was written by the node, so startup only checks a missing one.
- A symlinked `bootstore.json` is replaced by a regular file at the first save. A crash during a save can leave a `bootstore.json.*.tmp` behind. The directory isn't synced after the rename, so after a power loss the file may be the one from before the save.
- I couldn't run the docker recipe locally. Unrelated to this PR, it mounts the JWT at `/root/jwt` while the image runs as user 10001, which may not be able to read it.

### Alternatives

- Checking in `open` that the directory is writable, with a throwaway temporary file: rejected, as readers open the store too, and opening shouldn't write.
- Making the recipe's `/db` volume writable with a one-off service that `chown`s it as root: rejected as awkward next to mounting the node's home, which the image already owns.
- Review agents run: `rust-code-reviewer`, `deletion-reviewer`, and a general correctness and security review. Each finding fixed has its own commit. Dismissed:
  - the writability of an existing file (first caveat);
  - duplicate entries, or entries beyond 2048, in a hand-edited file don't mark the store dirty, so they stay in the file until the next change: the next PR reworks how records are added and can report these with the skipped ones;
  - the symlink, leftover temporary file and directory sync caveats above;
  - the "ENR Store Time" Grafana panel only sampling saves that wrote, which is intended;
  - the dev recipe's Dockerfile copying a Sepolia seed to a path nothing reads, which predates this PR;
  - the Korean configuration page, left to the translation-drift PRs.

### Follow-ups

- The rest of #23767, as stacked PRs: save only records that an outbound gossip connection verified, keep evidence timestamps per record and evict by them, and seed discovery from the saved records; then expire stale records.

Part of #23767.

topPRs.title: kona-registry!: require a dependency set and a known L1 for every custom-config chain
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
A custom-config Cannon prestate whose chain has no dependency set makes `kona-client-int` read local key 8 (`DEPENDENCY_SET_KEY`) at boot; a chain group on an L1 other than Ethereum mainnet, Sepolia or Holesky makes both kona-client programs read key 7 (`L1_CONFIG_KEY`). `addLocalData` loads only idents 1-4 (`SuperFaultDisputeGame`) or 1-5 (`FaultDisputeGame`) and `PreimageOracle.readPreimage` reverts for others, so the honest trace has a step nobody can prove onchain. Both are now build errors.

- The build also rejects a set that lists an unknown chain, or `interop` sections that declare a cluster matching no set. Each error names the custom file to fix.
- The checks live in `build_checks.rs`, shared by `build.rs` and an integration test, so CI's unit tests cover them. `just test` in `rust/` now also runs `test-custom-embeds`, which CI did not run before.
- Cannon and kona-sp1 builds now accept the same inputs: the SP1 ELF build already requires `depsets.json` and takes L1 configs only from the registry.
- Tags since `kona-node/v1.5.2` merge an optional `depsets.json`, so the docs apply to them; the Upgrade 20 and 21 notices say those tags do not check for it. Adding the file changes a prestate's hash, so reproduce an existing prestate with its original inputs. Korean docs sync via the translation-drift PRs.

BREAKING CHANGE: a custom-config prestate build (`KONA_CUSTOM_CONFIGS_DIR`) fails without `depsets.json`, or when a chain group is not on Ethereum mainnet, Sepolia or Holesky. A chain outside an interop cluster uses its self-only set, `[{"dependencies": {"<L2_CHAIN_ID>": {}}, "overrideMessageExpiryWindow": null}]`. A cluster uses one entry listing every member, identical to its dependency-set file (op-supernode's `--dependency-set`, else op-node's `--interop.dependency-set`) and op-challenger's depset config.

Part of https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/proofs-team/issues/62

topPRs.title: rust: make the reth forward sweep reviewable
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Makes the reth forward sweep reviewable. During the review of ethereum-optimism/reth#44, the sweep's report was session notes only, its range stopped before fixes that merged later, and several candidates had no recorded verdict.

- **`rust/scripts/reth-forward-prefilter.py`:** lists every fix, perf, security or revert commit newer than a fork pin, on upstream `main` and in newer release tags, deduplicated by patch id. For each it gives the first release containing it, whether the pin carries it as a hand-port, how many of its files exist at the pin, and whether it applies cleanly. It runs in seconds on a reth clone. Tests are in `just test-upstream-mirrors`.
- **Forward sweep in `docs/ai/reth-update-review.md`:**
  - Record the upstream tip.
  - Run the prefilter before reading.
  - Give every fix in range a verdict.
  - Re-sweep from the recorded tip before the fork PR merges.
  - Put the verdicts and the prefilter table in the fork PR.
  - Pick bar: by default, recommend a pick only for consensus or realistic node stability, argue other important fixes case by case, and allow watch items.
- **New "Reviewing a fork pick PR" checklist:** a range-diff per pick, a search for upstream reverts and follow-ups, and a rerun of the candidate list.
- **Re-sweep step:** also added to `UPDATING-RETH.md`, the `update-reth` skill and the reviewer agent.

Suggested by @aakoshh in the review of #24101.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topPRs.title: op-deployer!: reject artifacts-only contract layouts
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
Artifacts-only inputs still pass op-deployer's loaders after the Forge-only cutover, leaving operators to discover an unsupported setup later. This rejects those layouts when resolving locators and fixes `.tzst` downloads that discard the actual extraction directory. Artifact-relative filesystem paths remain unchanged for existing readers.

BREAKING CHANGE: users supplying artifacts-only directories or archives must switch to `embedded` or provide a complete built Forge project, including its configuration, sources, compile cache, and `forge-artifacts` directory. A local locator may still point at that project's `forge-artifacts` subdirectory.

Local lint, artifact race tests, non-embedded verifier tests, and op-deployer package compilation pass. The embedded-archive test and full deployment integration tests were not run. Go, deletion, test, and documentation review guidance was applied directly; separate reviewer agents were unavailable.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18346
